subject: Renewal: annualize remaining term and co-term flex path
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@brightlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: annualize remaining term and co-term flex path

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Based on BrightLabs’ trailing 60-day usage, I ran a quick set of options that can get you onto a single annual renewal (co-term) while preserving runway for the Q4 pilot you mentioned. High-level options below — I put the heuristic numbers in case procurement needs something to model quickly.

1) Annualize + modest uplift (recommended)
- Convert remaining 9 months into an annualized commitment
- Uplift applied to convert month-to-month consumption into committed units: ~15%
- One consolidated annual invoice (can be split into two instalments)
- Benefit: predictable unit price, no mid-contract trueup for the rest of the year

2) Staged top-up + credit smoothing
- Immediate top-up for current spike (3 months), then annualize for next 12 months
- Uplift on the top-up: ~20%, with a one-time promo credit (15% of top-up value) to offset timing pain
- Benefit: lower near-term cash but slightly higher long-run rate

3) Hybrid bridge (short-term loan style)
- Bridge with smaller immediate invoice, amortized credit over next 6 months
- Requires PO + short addendum

If procurement prefers invoice smoothing we can break invoices across quarters. I can generate a clean addendum draft and send a shoestring amortization schedule for finance.

To move fast: if BrightLabs is comfortable with Option 1, we can produce a single addendum and a proposed invoice schedule (annual or two-split). If Option 2, we’ll include the one-time credit and a clear trueup cadence.

Next steps:
- Which option does procurement prefer?
- If Option 1, can procurement confirm target invoice cadence (annual / 2x / quarterly)?
- I’ll loop in Finance to produce the addendum and amortization table.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@brightlabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightLabs Procurement <procurement@brightlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: annualize remaining term and co-term flex path

Ben —

Appreciate the options. Procurement is pushing for minimal near-term cash impact; two clarifying asks: 1) can you show actual invoice timing examples for Option 1 (annual vs 2-split vs quarterly) and 2) can you confirm whether a one-time credit of 30% on the immediate uplift is on the table (procurement asked explicitly).

We need the schedule and a clean addendum to share with legal by end of week.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Zhang
Head of Partnerships, BrightLabs
claire.zhang@brightlabs.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@brightlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: annualize remaining term and co-term flex path

Claire —

Thanks — looping in Marissa (AE lead) and Irene from Finance so we can get a concrete schedule and legal addendum moving. Attached is a simple spreadsheet with example invoice timing for Option 1 and Option 2 and an amortization column for the bridge approach.

Quick summary from Finance (high level):
- Option 1 (Annualize + 15% uplift)
  * Annual invoice amount = $540k (if we annualize remaining + next year at current runrate)
  * Payment cadence: annual, or split into 2 equal instalments (H1/H2); quarterly split increases processing overhead
- Option 2 (Staged top-up)
  * Immediate top-up invoice = $90k (3-month spike) with 15% one-time credit on the top-up amount if BrightLabs signs addendum within 10 business days
  * Following 12 months billed as committed annual at slightly reduced effective rate
- Bridge (amortized)
  * Immediate invoice reduced to $45k, remainder amortized over 6 months via credit schedule

Attachments: BrightLabs_Uplift_Options.xlsx (sheet: schedules & amortization).

If procurement is leaning toward the 30% ask, I should flag that as a concession that needs AE + RevOps approval; Finance prefers keeping a credit in the 10–20% band paired with a quicker signature turnaround. If procurement needs 30% to sign, let us know — we’ll route it for review.

Action items:
- Claire: procurement timeline + whether PO will be issued before legal completes addendum
- Marissa: can you prepare the addendum draft and proposed DocuSign flow?
- Irene: will review invoice split and confirm if 2x instalments are acceptable from accounting perspective.

Thanks —
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@brightlabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: annualize remaining term and co-term flex path

Claire / team —

Following up with concrete pricing options. I’ve pasted a short table below (numbers illustrative; final in the attached PDF):

Option A — Annualize (preferred)
- Commit: annualized amount based on current run-rate -> $540,000
- Upfront uplift: 15% applied to convert remaining months
- Credit: 10% one-time credit applied to the uplift if signed within 7 business days
- Invoice cadence: two-split instalment (50/50) recommended for cash smoothing

Option B — Staged top-up + credit
- Immediate top-up invoice: $90,000 (covers current spike)
- One-time credit on top-up: 15% if addendum signed within 10 business days; 30% would need RevOps sign-off and is exceptional
- Following 12 months: annualized contract at agreed committed rate

Operational notes:
- Legal prefers we execute a short addendum (attached) that references the existing MSA and the uplift schedule — this accelerates signature and minimizes redlines.
- If Procurement needs the PO first, we can accept a PO number and issue an invoice conditional on signed addendum; it slows the RevOps approval slightly.

Attachments: MA_Addendum_draft.pdf (contains redline-friendly placeholders), pricing appendix in-body.

Next steps: please indicate preferred option and procurement cadence. If you want to push for 30% credit, please confirm procurement is prepared to provide a signed PO within 3 business days so I can escalate to RevOps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@brightlabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: annualize remaining term and co-term flex path

Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the clear options and the addendum. Procurement reviewed and we can move forward on Option A (Annualize + 15% uplift) with the following conditions:

- BrightLabs will issue a PO referencing the addendum: PO-778912
- Invoice cadence requested: two instalments (50/50) with first invoice upon addendum signature and the second at 6 months
- We request the 10% one-time credit on the uplift as described in the addendum (accepted)
- Legal will review the attached MA_Addendum_draft and return any minor redlines by EOD Thursday

Please send the final addendum and DocuSign link and we’ll route the PO to finance.

Claire
Claire Zhang
Head of Partnerships, BrightLabs
claire.zhang@brightlabs.com
